title: Dedicated throughput assertion and autoscale-binding playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a single playbook and contract appendix that defines how Redwood quantifies and contracts dedicated throughput guarantees, how error budgets are computed, and the exact autoscale-binding grammar that ties a customer commitment to our autoscaler behavior. This ticket consolidates measurement windows, credit formulas, notification language, and operator runbooks for remediation. The output will be used by legal to produce SLAs and by engineering to implement telemetry and autoscale interlocks.
acceptance_criteria: A concise SLA appendix (<= 2 pages) that legal can embed in enterprise contracts describing measurable committed throughput, measurement window, and credit calculation
A deterministic error-budget formula with examples for common scenarios (AZ outage, gradual degradation, burst consumption)
Autoscale-binding spec that maps contract tiers to autoscaler intent and fallback policies (explicit names and thresholds)
Open-source-style metric names and query examples to compute committed throughput and SLO compliance
Sign-off by Legal, Head of Product, and Eng Reliability on remediation playbook and notification cadence
contract_clauses: Commitment: Customer is entitled to a committed serve rate measured as tokens-per-minute (TPM) over rolling 1-hour windows. Commitment tiers: Bronze (10k TPM), Silver (100k TPM), Gold (500k TPM).

Measurement: Compliance is evaluated using 95th percentile delivered throughput across 1-hour rolling windows over monthly billing period. Missed windows contribute to an error budget deficit computed as proportional shortfall.

Credit Calculation: For each hourly window where delivered throughput < committed throughput, compute shortfall_ratio = 1 - (delivered / committed). Customer credit for that hour = hourly_commitment_cost * shortfall_ratio. Monthly credit = sum(hourly credits) subject to cap at 100% of monthly committed charge.
Autoscale Interlock: When shortfall_ratio > 0.05 for 3 consecutive hourly windows, Redwood will trigger the autoscale remediation ladder and notify the customer per notice timelines below.

Notice & Remediation: Redwood will notify customers within 30 minutes of sustained degradation (>=3 consecutive failing windows) with an initial incident classification and expected remediation ETA. Credits are applied after remediation and final compliance calculation for the billing cycle.
measurement_spec: Primary metric: dedicated.serve_tokens.delivered.count (tags: customer_id, region, cluster_id, model_variant)
Windowing: compute delivered TPM by summing tokens in each 1-hour sliding window; slide frequency 5 minutes for early detection
Baseline adjustments: exclude throughput loss due to customer-side request throttling (verified by request logs) and force-maintenances declared at least 24h in advance
Aggregation: use 95th percentile across windows for monthly compliance reporting; hourly windows are used for credit math and escalation triggers

Example query (PromQL-like): sum_over_time(dedicated_serve_tokens_delivered{customer_id="C123"}[1h]) / 60
    // yields TPM for the 1h window
autoscale_binding_spec: Escalation ladder (automated): 1) aggressive vertical/burst autoscale attempt (fast path, <2m), 2) reserve additional nodes from warm pool (if available, <10m), 3) cross-AZ redistribution and optional model variant fallback (10-30m), 4) manual operator intervention

Policy binding semantics: contracts require Redwood to attempt autoscale remediation steps in order; credit is not waived by remediation attempts — credits are computed on delivered throughput vs commitment

Rate-limit interactions: when customer request rate exceeds configured burst_margin*committed_TPM, requests beyond capacity will receive 429 with structured metadata (retry-after, capacity-tier, fallback hints) to enable graceful degradation on customer side
telemetry_and_dashboards: Minimum dashboards: Committed TPM vs Delivered TPM (1h windows), Error budget burn rate, Autoscale events timeline, Node pool utilization by cluster
Alerting: SRE alert when shortfall_ratio > 0.10 sustained for 2 consecutive windows (pager), Warning when shortfall_ratio between 0.05 and 0.10 for 2 windows (email/console)
Audit logs: store autoscaler decisions and model fallback events tagged with incident_id and contract_tier for postmortem reconciliation
SLA report: monthly PDF with per-customer hourly compliance, credits applied, and event timeline exported to customer console and billing portal
open_decisions: Finalize default commitment tiers and pricing conversion for tokens-to-cost used in credit calculation (Finance input required)
Decide whether to use 1h rolling windows vs 30m for measurement (tradeoff detection sensitivity vs noise)
Agreement on minimum warm pool sizing policy and whether warm pool capacity is considered part of committed entitlement
Legal to confirm whether autoscale remediation attempts should be explicitly listed as conditions that reduce credits
